They get used interchangeably, but they're not the same thing. EFT (electronic funds transfer) is the general term in Canada for moving money electronically between bank accounts, including batch payments like payroll and pre-authorized debits, run through Payments Canada's systems. ACH is the name of the US clearing network, so the person on your call was either using it loosely for the Canadian batch EFT rails or talking about the US system. If it matters for a doc or slide, it's worth asking which they meant.

A heat warning means two or more days of high heat; an extended heat warning means it's expected to last three or more days. In southern Ontario the trigger is roughly daytime highs of 31 or more with overnight lows of 20 or more, or a humidex of 40 or higher. The precautions are the same, but with an extended one you should plan for several hot nights in a row and check on neighbours and relatives.

TL;DR: when kids use screens matters more than how much, and the hour before bed is the problem. In a 2025 study of 1,200 children aged 6 to 9, screens in the last 60 minutes meant falling asleep about 19 minutes later, worst with handheld devices and mildest with a shared living-room TV. The causes are light delaying melatonin, stimulating games and videos, and screens crowding out wind-down routines. The fix is a fixed screens-off time an hour before bed every night including weekends, devices charged outside the bedroom, and reading instead, which got sleep back to normal within about two weeks.
